question: A 42-year-old woman has 3 swollen MCPs and 2 swollen PIPs (>10 joints if counted bilaterally symmetrically, totalling 6 small joints), morning stiffness of 90 minutes, anti-CCP antibody high positive, and CRP elevated for 6 weeks. What is her 2010 ACR/EULAR RA classification criteria score?

answers.text: 3 points — does not meet the threshold for RA classification

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Incorrect scoring. Review the four domains: joint involvement, serology, acute-phase reactants, and symptom duration, each contributing points toward the ≥6/10 threshold.

answers.text: 6 points — just meets the threshold for RA classification

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Close, but the serology and joint categories in this case score higher. Recalculate: >10 small joints = 5 points (joint domain); high-positive anti-CCP = 3 points (serology); abnormal CRP = 1 point; ≥6 weeks duration = 1 point.

answers.text: 10 points — maximum possible score, clearly meeting RA classification

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Correct. Joint involvement: >10 joints (at least one small joint) = 5 points. Serology: high-positive anti-CCP = 3 points. Acute-phase reactant: abnormal CRP = 1 point. Duration: ≥6 weeks = 1 point. Total = 10/10. A score ≥6 classifies RA.

answers.text: 7 points — meets the threshold with moderate certainty

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Re-examine the scoring. The joint domain alone awards 5 points for >10 joints (with at least 1 small joint). Adding high-positive serology (3), abnormal CRP (1), and ≥6 weeks (1) reaches 10/10, not 7.

overallFeedback.feedback: 2010 ACR/EULAR RA criteria: (1) Joint involvement: 1 large=0, 2-10 large=1, 1-3 small=2, 4-10 small=3, >10 joints (≥1 small)=5. (2) Serology: negative=0, low-positive RF or anti-CCP=2, high-positive=3. (3) Acute-phase: normal CRP+ESR=0, abnormal=1. (4) Duration: <6w=0, ≥6w=1. ≥6 points classifies as RA.
Correct. This is a maximal-score case (10/10): joint domain 5 + serology 3 + APR 1 + duration 1. The threshold for RA classification is ≥6/10.
